clues: It opposes capillary hydrostatic pressure in the Starling forces governing fluid exchange.
Hypoalbuminemia in liver cirrhosis or nephrotic syndrome causes it to drop, leading to edema.
It is the osmotic pressure exerted by plasma proteins, primarily albumin, that keeps water inside blood vessels.
Despite having a pKa of 6.1, it is the most effective extracellular buffer in human blood.
A twenty-to-one ratio of its conjugate base to dissolved gas maintains arterial pH at 7.40.
It is an open physiological buffer regulated rapidly by the lungs and more slowly by the kidneys.
It is stored inside endothelial Weibel-Palade bodies and platelet alpha granules.
It circulates bound to Factor VIII to protect it from premature proteolytic degradation.
This multimeric glycoprotein bridges exposed subendothelial collagen to platelet GpIb receptors during primary hemostasis.
Low-dose aspirin prevents its synthesis for the entire lifespan of an anucleate blood cell.
Its vascular actions directly oppose those of endothelial prostacyclin.
This eicosanoid synthesized by platelet COX-1 stimulates vasoconstriction and platelet aggregation.

terms.sub: Coagulation Cascade and Vitamin K-Dependent Factors
clues: When bound to endothelial thrombomodulin, it switches from a procoagulant to an anticoagulant activator.
It activates Factors V, VIII, XI, and XIII as well as protease-activated receptors on platelets.
This central serine protease (Factor IIa) cleaves soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin monomers.

terms.sub: Coagulation Cascade and Vitamin K-Dependent Factors
clues: Deficiency of this factor causes delayed umbilical stump bleeding despite normal PT and aPTT results.
Unlike most clotting factors, it is a transglutaminase rather than a serine protease.
Activated by thrombin, it forms covalent crosslinks between fibrin polymers to stabilize the blood clot.
Inherited deficiency of this plasma protein causes resistance to standard unfractionated heparin therapy.
It is a hepatic serpin that neutralizes multiple activated coagulation serine proteases.
Heparin induces a conformational change in this inhibitor that accelerates its inactivation of thrombin and Factor Xa a thousand-fold.
Its deficiency can cause warfarin-induced skin necrosis during the first days of therapy due to its short half-life.
It is activated on intact endothelium by the thrombin-thrombomodulin complex.
Together with cofactor Protein S, this vitamin K-dependent protease inactivates Factors Va and VIIIa.
Drugs like alteplase and streptokinase work by promoting its generation from an inactive zymogen.
Aminocaproic acid and tranexamic acid inhibit its activity to control excessive bleeding.
This fibrinolytic serine protease digests crosslinked fibrin clots into soluble fragments including D-dimers.
